about: SEO Checker audits one public page and turns the result into a tabbed report: a Lighthouse SEO score, speed and Core Web Vitals, accessibility, HTTP headers, metadata, AI/LLM readiness, language signals and a best-guess technology stack. The Overview tab brings the six highest-impact fixes from every section to the top, so you know what to change first instead of reading dozens of audit cards.

Unlike the Trick-it tools that run entirely in the browser, this one has to reach out. A browser tab cannot render another site, read its response headers or fetch its robots.txt because of cross-origin rules, so the audit is run by services. When you start a check, the host asks you to confirm the exact URL and complete a Cloudflare Turnstile check. Google PageSpeed Insights then loads the page in its own browser to produce the Lighthouse results, and a bounded server-side read of the page, `/robots.txt` and `/llms.txt` supplies the headers, metadata, AI-readiness and language checks.

Because the tool is honest about what it measures, it is more useful as a checklist than as a ranking predictor. The SEO, speed and accessibility numbers are Google's Lighthouse category scores multiplied by 100. The headers, metadata, AI readiness and languages scores come from the tool's own published checklists. None of them estimates where a page will rank.

features.title: Seven score tiles
features.body: SEO, speed, accessibility, headers, AI readiness, languages and metadata are summarised on the Overview tab, followed by the six fixes that matter most across all sections.

features.title: Lab and field Core Web Vitals
features.body: The Speed tab shows Lighthouse lab metrics (LCP, FCP, CLS, TBT, Speed Index, TTFB and others) on range bars, together with Chrome UX Report field data where Google has it, plus the biggest opportunities and transfer size by resource type.

features.title: Header audit
features.body: Follows the redirect path and checks status, HTTPS, `X-Robots-Tag`, HSTS, weaknesses in Content-Security-Policy, CORS, nosniff, framing rules, referrer and permissions policy and caching headers.

features.title: Metadata and link preview
features.body: Checks title, description, canonical, robots, viewport, charset, favicon, Open Graph and Twitter cards, shows a text-only link preview, lists JSON-LD types and prints the heading outline.

features.title: AI / LLM readiness
features.body: Looks at AI crawler access in robots.txt, reachability, an `llms.txt` file, whether content is present in the static HTML, headings, structure, JSON-LD, metadata and authorship or dates.

features.title: Mobile or desktop strategy
features.body: Run the audit as a mobile or a desktop visitor. The Lighthouse device profile changes, so a page can score very differently on each.

reference.title: How the scores are built and what each tab checks

head: Score
Source
Method
rows: Lighthouse SEO category score x 100, rounded. A null result is an error, not a zero
Score x 100; metrics are rated against fixed thresholds
Score x 100, with failed audits grouped by area and manual checks listed separately
Weighted: pass counts 1, warning counts 0.5, fail counts 0; informational rules are excluded
Points earned divided by points available, rounded to 0 to 100

blocks.text: Manual, unavailable and not-applicable checks are never counted as passed. Title and description lengths are displayed for reference but are not scored, and the tool does not apply keyword-density rules.

Each lab metric is rated good, needs improvement or poor against the thresholds below, in milliseconds except CLS, which has no unit. These are the same boundaries Google publishes for Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) and Lighthouse (the others).

Lab data comes from one simulated load on Google's infrastructure. Field data, when shown, comes from real Chrome users over the previous period and is the figure Google uses for page experience. When they disagree, trust the field numbers and use the lab data to find the cause.

sections.heading: What the bounded page read does

items: GET requests only, with no cookies or credentials.
At most five redirects, with every hop re-validated: IP literals, internal names, embedded credentials, non-standard ports and non-HTTP(S) schemes are refused.
A 15 second timeout and a 512 kB cap on the document.
Only an allow-list of response headers is reported, and cookies are counted but never shown.
The service returns extracted facts, not the document, and the tool renders them as plain text.

blocks.text: If the page cannot be read, the Lighthouse sections still appear and the page-based sections explain why they are limited. Header findings come from one plain request, so a CDN or firewall that treats crawlers differently from browsers can produce results that differ from what a real visitor sees.

The AI tab checks whether content is reachable and legible without running JavaScript: is it in the static HTML, are headings and structured data present, does robots.txt block AI crawlers, and is there an `llms.txt`. The `llms.txt` check is labelled as an unconfirmed proposal, and the score does not claim that any provider ranks or cites pages by it. Treat it as a hygiene check for machine readability.

example.title: Auditing a product landing page before launch

items: Enter `https://shop.acme-studio.dev/` (the public page, not a staging link that needs a login), choose Mobile and confirm the URL and security check.
Wait while the status card counts elapsed time. An audit can take up to about 90 seconds.
On Overview, read the six top fixes. Suppose they include a missing meta description, an LCP of 4.8 s and no `Content-Security-Policy`.
Open Metadata to see the missing description and a text-only preview of how the title will look. Add the description and a canonical link.
Open Speed and read the opportunities list; a large hero image usually explains a slow LCP, so run it through [Image Compression](/image-compression/).
Open Headers, note that HSTS is missing, add it at the CDN and rerun. A new check clears the previous report so you never compare against stale data.

blocks.text: When you build social preview cards for the page, [OG Metadata Generator](/og-metadata-generator/) produces the tags the Metadata tab looks for.

limits: It needs internet access and Google's service to be available. Google's shared keyless quota can be exhausted, in which case the audit fails and you should retry later.
Only public URLs work. Pages behind a login, signed URLs and private hosts are refused, and you must never submit a link that contains a secret.
Each attempt is rate limited to five audits per 60 seconds per feature, approximately by IP and Cloudflare location, so users on a shared network share the allowance.
One page per run. It is not a site crawler and says nothing about sitewide indexing, backlinks, content quality or search intent.
Technology detection is a best guess from public signals, and a 100 score does not replace manual review.
The provider text is returned in English or Indonesian only. Other interface languages show English provider explanations.

faq.question: Is my URL sent anywhere?
faq.answer: Yes. The exact URL is sent to Google PageSpeed Insights, which loads the page, and to the Trick-it service that reads the page, robots.txt and llms.txt once. Cloudflare Turnstile verifies you are not a bot. You confirm all of this before the audit starts.

faq.question: Why is the Lighthouse score different from DevTools?
faq.answer: PageSpeed Insights runs on Google's servers with its own network and CPU throttling, while DevTools uses your machine. Expect differences, particularly in speed. The SEO score is far more stable.

faq.question: Does a score of 100 mean the page will rank?
faq.answer: No. The SEO category checks technical discoverability such as title, description, indexability, links, canonicals and image alternatives. It does not judge content usefulness or competition.

faq.question: Why did the audit fail with a quota or rate-limit message?
faq.answer: Either you made more than five checks in a minute, or Google's shared PageSpeed quota was used up. Wait a minute and retry; if it persists, try later.

faq.question: Which pages can I check?
faq.answer: Any public HTTP or HTTPS page on a normal port. Credentials in the URL, local or private hostnames and unusual ports are rejected.

faq.question: How do I fix broken links or redirects it finds?
faq.answer: Use [Link Checker](/link-checker/) to inspect suspicious or redirecting URLs passively, and [HAR Studio](/har-studio/) to examine a full network capture of a slow page.
